newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas falls sharply, retraces from recent high.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas falls sharply, retraces from recent high.

text.p: UK spot natural gas markets were extremely volatile on Thursday, traders and brokers said, as a penny or more a therm was wiped off values in the early afternoon before prices later bounced and recovered some of the losses.
All periods still ended the day down by around 0.70 pence a therm

There were some notable trading coups as prices bounced around. One trader bought a 50,000 therm lot in the gas year from October 1997 at 12.80 pence a therm, and then immediately resold 25,000 therms of this at 13.10 pence. The same trader bought Q1 1998 at 16.30 pence and sold the same volume in the same period at 17.10 pence.

While some dealers were delighted with the opportunities provided by the volatility, producers were less certain. One said that with prices bouncing around, people were only interested in trading their books rather than buying gas for consumption.

"People are too interested in shenanigans at the NBP to buy real gas," he said. "Somebody's obviously lost their shirt and somebody's obviously gained it. If you're a trader that's what you're there for, but not if you're a producer."

Others agreed the market had been hard to follow. "It's been a really choppy day," said one. "It's been difficult to peg where numbers were. You couldn't place numbers as it moved so quickly. The dust has yet to settle."

The fall was seen as a retracement from recent highs, as the market had climbed over several days at the end of last week and the beginning of this. "People have been saying it's overheated for ages," said one trader.

Although levels had started to come off over the last day or two, it was only on Thursday that the retracement picked up real momentum. One or two large sellers were said to have been aggressively offering, and were seen by many as responsible for much of the fall.
The trading ranges over the day were wide. The gas year from October was reported traded at a high of 13.85 pence and a low of 12.80 pence.
There was also a lot of volatility in the fourth quarter, trading between 13.50 pence and 14.10 pence. The first quarter also saw a wide range.

Spot market falls had an impact on the IPE futures market. Although there was no trade in the afternoon, during a week in which extremely little has been done, bids and offers came down swiftly in line with the OTC market.

March 1998 settled at 14.695 pence a therm, a loss of 0.910 penny, the biggest of the day. But there were also some other big falls, with several months posting losses of over 0.80 penny on the previous settlement level.
Front month June settled at 11.07 pence a therm, down 0.510 pence on the day.
